survey: A satellite-dish tower standing in a desert, seen from a three-quarter view, slightly from above. From the bottom up: (1) A square stone slab lies flat on the sand. Its top face is wide open to view, and its left and right edges run roughly parallel down to a near corner at the lower left. (2) A tapered grey cone stands on the slab. Its base meets the slab in a downward-curving ellipse, which agrees with a view from above. A riveted access plate is flat on the side facing the camera and follows the cone's curve. (3) A riveted metal collar sits on top of the cone. It is drawn showing its top face, with a dark inner ring and a lower edge that curves down. (4) A box-shaped yoke rises out of the collar. Its pivot bolt points at the camera, so the dish tilts within the picture plane, which is consistent. (5) The dish is a white bowl with its inside facing up and to the left. Its rim is a narrow ellipse whose long axis runs from lower left to upper right, with the rim's thickness showing along the lower-left edge. Three struts hold the feed: two legs land on the inside of the bowl near its left rim, and one horizontal bar runs to the far right rim. They meet at a feed head with a red dome above the dish's upper left, roughly along the dish's axis. (6) The background is a flat desert with its horizon at about the middle of the cone in the enlarged view.

errors.where: Upper tower (collar, yoke top, feed head) compared with the horizon
errors.what: The desert horizon sits at about the middle of the cone, which puts the camera's eye level there. The collar, the yoke and the red-domed feed head are all well above that line. They should show their undersides, with ellipses curving upward. Instead they are drawn from above: the collar's top face and inner ring are visible, its lower edge curves down, and the top of the dome is visible. The ground and slab use a high camera, while the low horizon implies a camera at mid-tower height.

fix: Use a single high camera looking down on the whole tower: lower the desert horizon so it sits near the top of the image, above the dish, so that the slab, cone, collar, yoke and dish are all seen from above. Alternatively, keep the horizon at mid-tower and draw the collar, yoke and feed head from slightly below, with the collar's underside visible and its ellipses curving upward.
